title: Questions, what we have, what we do not have, and what it blocks
rule: A question is closed only when its closing test is met by published evidence. Until then the decision it blocks is not made.

questions.question: Which book, or which composite, is 'the market line'?
questions.have: 20,336 market rows in the price store, but 0 of them name a book on the closing snapshot; the only named vendor is the code WSGT, on the 2021 initial-lines file.
questions.missing: a book identifier on every closing price row
questions.blocks: beat-the-close reporting, any claim that a fair line differs from a market a person could actually bet into, and gate G0 for every strategy
questions.closing_test: every new closing row carries a book code that maps to a named sportsbook in a registry, and two independent captures of the same book agree on the number

questions.question: When was each number captured?
questions.have: 0 rows with a timestamp. The publisher's files have no time column at all, so 'opening' and 'closing' are inferences from a file name and a row order.
questions.missing: a capture timestamp on every snapshot
questions.blocks: true closing-line value (CLV), the demotion trigger D-03, and the opening-vs-closing column for any game
questions.closing_test: two snapshots of the same market on the same day, both timestamped, show the line moving

questions.question: Why do two nflverse files disagree about the closing spread?
questions.have: closing_lines.csv and games.csv agree on 2,267 games and disagree on 1,101 after normalising the documented sign convention (32.7%).
questions.missing: the publisher's statement of which file is authoritative, or a licensed feed that settles it
questions.blocks: choosing the benchmark the model is scored against
questions.closing_test: a third, independent source agrees with one of the two on a sample of at least 100 games

questions.question: Is the originated line good enough to bet against a real market?
questions.have: Side MAE 10.741 vs market 9.792; total MAE 11.102 vs 10.447; Brier 0.241 vs 0.212 on 3,165 out-of-sample games. The model beats a constant home-field baseline and loses to the market on every metric.
questions.missing: information the market does not have, or a documented inefficiency to exploit
questions.blocks: staking anything; promoting any strategy out of paper
questions.closing_test: a strategy's out-of-sample z clears 1.96 with a bootstrap interval excluding the break-even, on a pre-registered window

questions.question: Should the injury/deficiency signal enter the line at all?
questions.have: 37 certain starter replacements, 34 at the second string, 0 at the third; 15 depth losses among backups; and no measurement of what any of it does to the score.
questions.missing: a coefficient: the effect of a replacement's depth on the margin, estimated out of sample on at least two seasons
questions.blocks: using T16 as an input rather than a report
questions.closing_test: the coefficient's out-of-sample interval excludes zero and the line model's MAE improves when it is added

questions.question: Is Phi(margin / sigma) a valid map from our spread to a win probability?
questions.have: The moneyline derived from the side wins 34.7% of 2,743 decided tickets against a per-ticket bar of 36.1%, and 29.6% on competitive-margin games (z = -4.5). The selections are mostly underdogs, because that is where the model disagrees with the price.
questions.missing: a calibrated spread-to-probability map, fitted on realised outcomes rather than assumed normal
questions.blocks: publishing a moneyline at all, and any moneyline-based strategy
questions.closing_test: a reliability curve for the win probability whose slope is in [0.85, 1.15] and whose Brier beats the market-implied probability

questions.question: Should a positive ROI with a weak signal ever be staked?
questions.have: 1 strategy shows a positive ROI (two-leg side parlay, +10.5%) and its signal z is 1.00 against a 1.96 bar. It is demoted on drawdown (52.7% vs a 25% cap) and on price loss.
questions.missing: a rule: whether the ROI may be surfaced at all when the signal fails
questions.blocks: the definition of 'live' on the leaderboard
questions.closing_test: the owner picks a policy from S-L2 and it is written into the gate

questions.question: What is a reward, and who pays it?
questions.have: eight candidate strategies, none live, no reward mechanism and no funding.
questions.missing: a reward definition (rank? payout? scrip?) and whether any real money is involved, which has legal consequences this repository cannot assess
questions.blocks: the rewards column on the leaderboard
questions.closing_test: a written reward rule, reviewed for legality by someone qualified to do so

questions.question: What is the correlation between two legs of a real parlay?
questions.have: margin vs total r = 0.0216 (n = 7,413); side vs market r = -0.4262 (n = 7,413); 49 values in total, each with n and an interval.
questions.missing: player-prop leg correlations and same-player stat correlations
questions.blocks: pricing a prop combo, and gate G7 for any parlay involving props
questions.closing_test: a paired prop dataset for two seasons produces a value whose interval excludes zero

questions.question: Should the pipeline depend on a source this environment cannot reach?
questions.have: nfl.com is unreachable from this sandbox (HTTP 000); nflverse release assets redirect to a blocked host; the nflverse repository archive is reachable and pinned by SHA-256.
questions.missing: a decision on whether to fund a licensed feed, or to keep the reproducible-but-limited GitHub path
questions.blocks: prop markets, player stats beyond the box score, multi-season injury history
questions.closing_test: either a licence is recorded, or the lab publishes a written limitation statement that the owner accepts

questions.question: Why can't the injury report be read in bulk?
questions.have: the Week 10 report is present via a previous session's collection (345 rows); this session could not re-fetch nfl.com to re-verify a single one of them.
questions.missing: a reachable official injury endpoint or an archived weekly series
questions.blocks: re-verifying the injury rows, and the two-season injury history that Q-M2 needs
questions.closing_test: the pipeline fetches an official injury page at run time and the fetched rows diff clean against the published ones

questions.question: What counts as 'official' for a betting price?
questions.have: no NFL or club source publishes a betting price, so every price row in this repository is second-hand by construction. The existing site's rule requires an official source on every data row.
questions.missing: a written exception that names the acceptable second-hand publishers and the verification each one gets
questions.blocks: publishing any price at all without breaking the site's own rule, or relaxing the rule silently
questions.closing_test: the source registry lists a price tier with its publisher, licence status and the check performed on it
